evals.prompt: Help me merge origin/feature/tenant-migration into the current branch, and confirm whether the initialization chain and config write-back were missed.
evals.behaviour_prompt:
Help me merge origin/feature/tenant-migration into the current branch, and confirm whether the initialization chain and config write-back were missed. What I have so far:

$ git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD
release/3.2
$ git status --short
(clean)
$ git fetch origin && git merge-base HEAD origin/feature/tenant-migration
9c41e07
$ git rev-list --left-right --count HEAD...origin/feature/tenant-migration
3	5
$ git log --oneline HEAD..origin/feature/tenant-migration
a81f2d4 tenant: add TenantMode.SHARDED and route it in the request filter
5be0c19 tenant: write shard map back to config on first boot
c07d3e2 tenant: migration script for tenant_shard table
e44a1b8 tenant: default shard count in defaults.yaml
f1290aa test: shard-map write-back unit test

Files changed on both sides since the merge base: src/tenant/bootstrap.py, config/defaults.yaml.
On release/3.2, bootstrap.py gained an init_quota() step before init_tenant_mode(), and defaults.yaml renamed tenant.mode to tenant.default_mode.
On the source side, init_tenant_mode() now calls load_shard_map(), and defaults.yaml adds tenant.mode: sharded and tenant.shard_count: 8.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger safe-merge-review. The result should first lock down the source ref and the current branch, model the merge base, left/right counts, incoming commits, and hotspot files, then provide a completeness proof, the minimal relevant verification, and a push decision.

evals.prompt: I'm not confident about this merge commit; help me review whether Git merged it but the logic is actually wired up wrong, especially the deploy config and schema changes.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger safe-merge-review. The result should recognize the task as auditing a completed merge, not directly merging again; it should reconstruct the expected diff, check the deploy config, schema, and shared boundaries, and produce a Green/Yellow/Red conclusion.

evals.prompt: The release branches in these repos all need merging; help me confirm per repo which repos genuinely have incoming commits and which repos already include them.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger safe-merge-review. The result should recognize the request as a multi-repo coordinated merge and output evidence per repo, rather than covering all repos with a single unified statement.

evals.prompt: For this conflicted file, help me decide whether to keep ours or theirs, and after resolving it can I actually push?

$ git diff config/retry.yaml
<<<<<<< HEAD

evals.expected_output: Should trigger safe-merge-review. The result should require looking at the base, ours, theirs three-way evidence, explain the conflict resolution, and give a push recommendation only after a completeness proof and the minimal relevant verification.

evals.prompt: Help me write a Python merge sort, and explain the time complexity while you're at it.
evals.expected_output: Should not trigger safe-merge-review; this is not a branch merge, merge audit, or conflict review task.

evals.prompt: I used a squash merge to bring feature/payment in; help me verify whether the changes really landed completely, and don't use is-ancestor.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger safe-merge-review. The result should recognize this as a squash merge audit, use the patch-equivalent or tree-diff method to verify completeness, and annotate proof-method in the evidence, without using is-ancestor.

evals.prompt: There are uncommitted changes right now; help me merge origin/hotfix/db-lock in.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger safe-merge-review. The result should detect the dirty worktree, stop or escalate for confirmation, state the risk, and require the user to handle the uncommitted changes first, rather than directly running the merge.

evals.prompt: Help me merge that branch, you know, the most recent line.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger safe-merge-review. The result should refuse to guess the source ref, require the user to explicitly provide a branch name or remote ref, and not start the merge directly from a vague description.

evals.prompt: We keep 5.1 and 5.2 as parallel release lines. A fix landed on 5.2, but is-ancestor and searching the commit id and the issue number on 5.1 all report it as missing. Confirm whether 5.1 really contains that fix.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger safe-merge-review. The result should recognize parallel, independent baseline lines where the same logical change lands via a different commit and issue id per line, so is-ancestor, commit-id search, and issue-number search can all falsely report missing. It should judge containment by file content / patch equivalence rather than the commit graph or issue id, and annotate the proof-method used.

evals.prompt: Review my branch's code changes for bugs and style before I open a PR. Nothing is being merged yet.
evals.expected_output: Should not trigger safe-merge-review; there is no merge, merge audit, or conflict to reason about. This is general pre-PR code review (code style and correctness), so safe-merge-review should not drive it; it applies once a merge, merge audit, or conflict resolution is actually in play.

evals.prompt: Here's the merge request: https://gitlab.example.com/team/backend/-/merge_requests/482 . Before I click merge, confirm the source branch is safe to bring into my current branch and that nothing on the shared config boundary was missed.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger safe-merge-review. From the merge request link the result should resolve the source ref and the target/current branch, fetch and model the diff (merge base, left/right counts, incoming commits, hotspot overlap on the shared config), do a semantic pre-review, and give a Green/Yellow/Red verdict with an explicit merge decision rather than blindly clicking merge; any trial merge runs in a disposable worktree, and nothing is merged, committed, or pushed in the user's worktree. It should not defer this to a general MR-creation (gitlab) or a pre-PR code-review skill, because a merge-correctness proof is in play.

evals.prompt: 帮我把 origin/release-2.6 合并到当前分支,冲突解完以后确认没有漏掉对面分支的改动,再决定要不要推上去。
evals.expected_output: Should trigger safe-merge-review from Chinese-language phrasing. The run should model the diff before merging, review conflict hotspots, produce a completeness proof that no incoming change was lost, and end with an explicit push decision.

evals.prompt: 帮我 review 一下这个分支的代码质量,暂时还不打算合到主干。
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger safe-merge-review; this is a pre-merge code-quality review with no merge in play (Chinese-language phrasing), so it routes to a code-review workflow instead.

evals.prompt: 这个分支改动很干净、测试也全绿,但它注册了一个 skill,而这个 skill 的源码在另一个仓库、还没推到我们 config 追踪的那个 ref 上。现在能合进主分支吗?
evals.expected_output: Should trigger safe-merge-review. The result should recognize that a clean diff with a green test run is not sufficient when the change registers or references an externally-sourced artifact whose source is not yet published on the ref the config tracks, and that the diff's own tests may only assert configuration shape and never exercise the real failure mode. It should gate the merge on the referenced artifact being published on the tracked ref (for example via git ls-remote), trace the downstream consumer and simulate the post-merge pipeline by reading it, and withhold the push decision until that is proven.

evals.prompt: 这个分支做了哪些变更,评估一下是否适合合入主分支?
evals.behaviour_prompt:
这个分支做了哪些变更,评估一下是否适合合入主分支?以下是我已经拿到的信息:

$ git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD
feature/export-csv
$ git fetch origin && git merge-base HEAD origin/main
4d2e9a0
$ git rev-list --left-right --count origin/main...HEAD
6	4
$ git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD
b7c1e20 export: add CSV export endpoint /api/reports/export
c3a9f41 export: stream rows instead of loading whole report
d05e8b2 export: add export permission check
e1f7a33 test: export endpoint happy path

两边自合并基点以来都改过的文件: src/reports/service.py, src/auth/permissions.py。
origin/main 的 6 个提交里,有一个把 permissions.py 里的 can_view_report(user, report) 改成了 can_view_report(user, report, tenant);本分支 d05e8b2 新增的导出权限检查仍按两个参数调用它。
evals.expected_output: Should trigger safe-merge-review. This is a pre-merge go/no-go suitability review — deciding whether a branch is ready to be merged into the main branch — which is in scope. The result should model the diff (source ref, merge base, incoming commits, hotspot overlap), do a semantic pre-review, and give a verification-backed recommendation on whether it is safe to merge — here the stale two-argument can_view_report call — without merging or committing in the user's worktree, rather than treating it as a general branch code-quality review with no merge in play.

evals.prompt: 帮我把这个函数里重复的三段逻辑抽成一个私有方法,当前分支上直接改。
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger safe-merge-review. No merge, merge audit, or conflict resolution is in play — this is an in-place refactor of existing code on the current branch, which belongs to change-discipline. safe-merge-review only applies once two lines of history have to be reconciled or a merge's completeness proved.

evals.prompt: 给我看看这个仓库最近一周有哪些提交,谁提交的。
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger safe-merge-review. Listing recent commits and their authors is a plain history query answerable with git log; nothing is being merged, audited for completeness, or resolved. Loading a merge-proof workflow for a read-only history lookup is over-application.

evals.prompt: 这个 feature 分支之前是 squash 进来的。我在当前工作树里 cherry-pick --no-commit 原提交时只剩冲突,这能证明改动已经完整包含了吗?
evals.expected_output: Should trigger safe-merge-review. Conflicts are inconclusive: they can come from different target-side changes and do not prove that the source patch is present. The result should reject the current-worktree stash/cherry-pick recipe, use an isolated disposable worktree if a cherry-pick no-op check is still needed, accept only a clean successful application with no index or worktree diff as a no-op, and otherwise fall back to file-content or patch-equivalent evidence.
